kaps_punt: Suid-Afrika het 'n besonder ryk fossielrekord van plante, diere en vroeë mense; belangrike fossiele wat in Suid-Afrika aangetref word, sluit in die Coelacanth en Afrikaanse dinosourusse; die "Wieg van die mensdom" is een van die plekke waar belangrike fossiele van die mensdom in Suid-Afrika gevind is

items.bewering: Mense het in ons land al baie fossiele van plante en van diere gevind. Hulle het ook fossiele van vroeë mense in die rotse gevind.
items.bron: Wits Evolutionary Studies Institute (wits.ac.za/esi): collections of dinosaurs, therapsids, plants and fossil hominids; South African Journal of Science review (sajs.co.za) on the hominin record.

items.bewering: Ons land se fossielrekord is besonder ryk aan al drie hierdie groepe. Dit beteken daar is hier baie fossiele en ook baie soorte.
items.bron: South African Strategy for the Palaeosciences (DST, 2011; up.ac.za copy) names a geographical advantage 'owing to the quantity and diversity of finds'; Deputy Minister Hanekom budget vote speech 16 May 2012 (gov.za): 'some of the richest evidence' of plant and animal evolution and human origins. 'Besonder ryk' is an intensifier, not a ranking, and is supported.

items.bewering: Hulle is boonop op baie verskillende plekke in ons land gevind.
items.bron: The lesson's own sites span the Karoo basin, Makhanda (Waterloo Farm, Eastern Cape; Gess & Coates 2015, sciencedaily.com) and the Cradle of Humankind (Gauteng; sahistory.org.za).

items.bewering: Al die fossiele van 'n land vorm saam sy fossielrekord.
items.bron: The standard meaning of 'fossil record' is the whole body of fossils and what they record. Applying it to one country is the ordinary usage in the palaeosciences strategy above ('South Africa's fossil record').

items.bewering: Fossiele lê byna altyd in die lae van sedimentêre rots.
items.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
items.bron: UC Museum of Paleontology fossil education pages (ucmp.berkeley.edu) and Rochester Academy of Science stratigraphy page (rasny.org): fossils are found mostly in sedimentary rock. 'Byna altyd' correctly leaves room for exceptions such as amber, ice and volcanic ash.

items.bewering: Groot dele van ons land lê juis op sedimentêre rots. Die Karoo is een van daardie dele, en dit is 'n baie groot gebied.
items.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
items.bron: Karoo Supergroup: a sedimentary sequence covering almost two-thirds of southern Africa's present land surface (Wikipedia 'Karoo Supergroup', citing the geological literature); Iziko Museums 'Karoo palaeontology' (iziko.org.za).

items.bewering: Ons land het dus baie van die regte soort rots vir fossiele om in te lê.
items.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
items.bron: Follows from the two items above; Iziko Museums on the Karoo's rich vertebrate fossil record (iziko.org.za).

items.bewering: Fossiele van dinosourusse uit Afrika is ook hier in ons land gevind. Hierdie dinosourusse het in Afrika geleef, lank voordat daar mense was.
items.bron: Wits ESI dinosaur collections (wits.ac.za/esi); Karoo Supergroup upper strata (Elliot and Clarens Formations, Late Triassic to Early Jurassic) carry dinosaur fossils (Wikipedia 'Karoo Supergroup'). Dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, long before humans. Note for the writer, not a fault: at the time the land was part of Pangaea/Gondwana, so 'in Afrika' means the land that is now Africa, which is acceptable at Grade 5.

items.bewering: Party van die fossiele is bene en tande wat in die rots bly lê het. Ander is spore wat 'n dier lank gelede in sagte modder getrap het.
items.bron: Dinosaur trackways from the Elliot Formation in South Africa: Mafube, Free State (over 80 tridactyl tracks; PeerJ 2285, peerj.com/articles/2285) and Storm Shelter, Eastern Cape (sajs.co.za). Bones: Wits ESI dinosaur collections.

items.bewering: Wetenskaplikes het lank net fossiele van visse soos die Coelacanth geken. Hulle het nie verwag om so 'n vis lewend in die see te sien nie.
items.bron: Natural History Museum London, 'Coelacanths: the fish that outdid the Loch Ness monster' (nhm.ac.uk): known only from fossils and thought extinct for about 66 million years before 1938.

items.bewering: In 1938 is 'n lewende Coelacanth voor die kus van ons land gevang.
items.bron: Australian Museum, Latimeria chalumnae (australian.museum); NHM London (nhm.ac.uk): caught by Captain Goosen's trawler off the Chalumna River near East London, December 1938. The fish was alive when landed.

items.bewering: Die nuus daaroor het die hele wêreld verras.
items.bron: NHM London (nhm.ac.uk) and History Today, 'Discovery of a living fossil' (historytoday.com): the find was a worldwide sensation and gave rise to the name 'living fossil'.

items.bewering: Die Coelacanth is 'n groot vis wat diep in die see lewe.
items.bron: FishBase, Latimeria chalumnae (fishbase.se/summary/2063): up to 168 cm (males) and 200 cm (females), up to 95 kg; depth 150-700 m, usually 180-250 m.

items.bewering: Die vis wat gevang is, lyk baie soos die diere in daardie fossiele. Hy wys hoe 'n fossiel en 'n dier wat vandag lewe, by mekaar pas.
items.bron: NHM London (nhm.ac.uk); Australian Museum (australian.museum): the living fish closely resembles fossil coelacanths in its overall body plan. The comparison is safe as written because it says 'lyk baie soos' and does not say 'dieselfde' or 'het nooit verander nie'. It must not be tightened into 'dieselfde vis as in die fossiele', because modern Latimeria is a different species from every known fossil coelacanth.

items.bewering: Naby Makhanda in die Oos-Kaap is ook fossiele van ander soorte Coelacanth in die rots gevind, soorte wat lank gelede uitgesterf het.
items.bron: Gess & Coates 2015, Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 175(2):360 (academic.oup.com); ScienceDaily 21 September 2015 (sciencedaily.com); Grocott's Mail, Rhodes University (grocotts.ru.ac.za). The Waterloo Farm site near Makhanda has yielded more than 30 specimens of ONE extinct coelacanth species, Serenichthys kowiensis, about 360 million years old (Late Devonian), Africa's earliest known coelacanth. No source found describes a second coelacanth species from the site. The location, the extinction and the fact that fossil coelacanths were found there are all correct. Only the plural 'soorte' is not supported.
items.regstelling: Narrow the plural to the singular: near Makhanda fossils of ONE other kind of coelacanth were found, a kind that died out long ago. Everything else in the sentence (Makhanda, Eastern Cape, in the rock, long extinct) is correct and should stay. Do not add a number of years or a species name unless it is needed.

items.bewering: Die Wieg van die Mensdom is 'n werklike plek in Gauteng.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Cradle of Humankind' (sahistory.org.za); Wikipedia 'Cradle of Humankind': about 50 km north-west of Johannesburg in Gauteng. Note for the writer, not a fault: the landscape extends a little into North West Province. 'In Gauteng' is the standard description and is acceptable, but a learner should not be taught that none of it lies outside Gauteng.

items.bewering: Dit is 'n gebied met baie grotte in 'n soort rots wat ons dolomiet noem.
items.bron: Review of the geomorphology and stratigraphy of the Sterkfontein Caves (literature.wolkersdorfer.info, PDF): the hominid-bearing caves sit in exposed, karstified dolomite; sahistory.org.za.

items.bewering: Navorsers het in daardie grotte al baie fossiele van vroeë mense gevind.
items.bron: sahistory.org.za: Sterkfontein, Swartkrans, Kromdraai and others; Mrs Ples (Australopithecus africanus) found at Sterkfontein in 1947. South African Tourism press page (southafrica.net): about 40% of the world's known hominid fossils come from the Cradle. 'Vroeë mense' follows CAPS's own wording for hominin fossils, which include human ancestors that were not Homo.

items.bewering: Die plek het sy naam gekry omdat soveel van hierdie fossiele juis daar gevind is.
items.bron: South African Tourism press page 'Cradle of Humankind: the birthplace of the human family' (southafrica.net): the name reflects the concentration of early hominin finds (about 40% of the world's known hominid fossils). No source found records who chose the name, but the stated reason matches every source's description.

items.bewering: Dit is een van die plekke in ons land met sulke fossiele.
items.bron: UNESCO's 'Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa' also takes in Taung (North West) and Makapan Valley (Limpopo) besides the Cradle (Wikipedia 'Cradle of Humankind', sahistory.org.za).

items.bewering: Die Wieg is vandag 'n Wêrelderfenisgebied, en die grotte word beskerm.
items.bron: sahistory.org.za, 'The Fossil Hominid Sites of Sterkfontein, Swartkrans, Kromdraai, and Environs': inscribed by UNESCO in 1999, listed today as 'Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa'.

items.bewering: Hierdie fossiele vertel ons watter plante en diere lank gelede hier geleef het. Hulle wys ook in watter dele van ons land vroeë mense geleef het.
items.bron: Iziko Museums 'Karoo palaeontology' (iziko.org.za); sahistory.org.za on the Cradle; South African Strategy for the Palaeosciences.

items.bewering: Navorsers van regoor die wêreld kom hierheen om die fossiele te bestudeer.
items.bron: Wits ESI (wits.ac.za/esi) describes its fossil collections as internationally acclaimed; University of Potsdam field report from Sterkfontein, May 2015 (uni-potsdam.de) is one instance of foreign research teams working in the Cradle.

items.bewering: Elke nuwe fossiel vertel iets meer oor die lewe van lank gelede.
items.bron: This is a general statement about what fossils are for, consistent with every source above. It has no specific content that could be false.

items.bewering: fossielrekord: Al die fossiele wat in 'n plek se rotse bewaar gebly het.
items.bron: Matches the standard meaning of the term (the total of preserved fossils and what they record); UCMP Berkeley fossil education pages. It reads correctly on its own and agrees with the study block's 'Al die fossiele van 'n land vorm saam sy fossielrekord'.

items.bewering: Coelacanth: 'n Groot vis wat diep in die see lewe en baie soos visse in fossiele lyk. Wetenskaplikes het net daardie fossiele geken totdat 'n lewende een in 1938 gevang is.
items.bron: FishBase (fishbase.se/summary/2063) for size and depth; NHM London (nhm.ac.uk) and Australian Museum (australian.museum) for 'known only from fossils' until the December 1938 catch.

items.bewering: dolomiet: 'n Sedimentêre rots wat baie soos kalksteen lyk.
items.bron: Rochester Academy of Science stratigraphy page (rasny.org): dolostone is a calcium magnesium carbonate sedimentary rock, closely related to calcium carbonate limestone. 'Lyk baie soos' is true. The definition does not claim they are the same rock, and it should not be changed to say so.

items.bewering: Wêrelderfenisgebied: 'n Plek wat vir die hele wêreld belangrik is, op die amptelike wêreldlys staan en beskerm word.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Convention: sites of 'outstanding universal value' inscribed on the World Heritage List, which the states that hold them undertake to protect (whc.unesco.org; summarised for the Cradle at sahistory.org.za).

opsomming: One fault: the Coelacanth block says fossils of other KINDS (plural) of coelacanth were found near Makhanda, but the sources describe only one extinct species from that site (Serenichthys kowiensis, about 360 million years old). Narrow it to the singular. Every other claim checked out, including 1938, the Karoo, the Cradle's dolomite caves and its 1999 World Heritage listing.
